s8ARemediation.fix: structureInputHash now includes STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION (imported as a value from types.ts).
s8ARemediation.beforeAfterProof: With unchanged text but a mocked STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION bump (v1->v2), the persisted inputHash changes, attemptCount increments (real recompute, not resume), and the new algorithm's output actually surfaces ('6.02' now present), matching fresh persisted DocumentNode rows.

s8BRemediation.rootCause: amendmentsInputHash = hashParts(documents.map(d => d.label)) - keyed on label only, while the real runAmendmentsStage scans both d.label AND d.text.slice(0, 2000).
s8BRemediation.fix: amendmentsInputHash now hashes `${d.label}:${d.text}` per document (deliberately the full text, not just the 2000-char window the stage reads - justified as a correctness-over-precision tradeoff since AMENDMENTS is a free deterministic scan, so over-invalidation costs nothing real).
s8BRemediation.beforeAfterProof: Same documentId/label, text changed to an amendment-shaped preamble: inputHash changes, attemptCount increments, orchestrator's AMENDMENTS stage now reports REVIEW_REQUIRED, matching a fresh direct call to the same function (previously silently stayed COMPLETED/stale).
s8BRemediation.acceptedTradeoff: A whitespace-only text edit that does NOT affect amendment detection will still force recompute under this fix - an explicit, documented, deliberate over-invalidation trade-off, not a smart content-fingerprint, justified by the stage's zero real cost.

s8DReplayEquivalence.proof: For both STRUCTURE and AMENDMENTS stages: an unchanged-input second call left attemptCount and inputHash identical, and the real stage function was never re-invoked (proven via vi.fn() call count for STRUCTURE), with output byte-identical to the fresh run - both directions of 8D proven (fresh vs. replay equivalence when unchanged; forced recompute when a relevant input changes).
